question: What is the primary goal of the MPDSR process in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To prevent future maternal and perinatal deaths through systematic review
options.B: To punish healthcare workers who make clinical errors during delivery
options.C: To collect accurate census data for the national government
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of running maternity wards

explanation: MPDSR focuses on understanding why deaths occur so that corrective actions can be put in place to save future lives. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is MPDSR considered especially important within the Nigerian healthcare context?

options.A: Midwives have extra free time to complete paperwork during night shifts
options.B: International donors require every clinic to submit monthly handwritten reports
options.C: Nigerian hospitals do not record any other types of patient statistics
options.D: Maternal and perinatal mortality ratios remain critically high across the country

explanation: Because Nigeria faces a heavy burden of maternal and newborn deaths, tracking and analyzing these events is essential for saving lives. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h1)

question: Within what timeframe should a maternal or perinatal death ideally be notified after it occurs?

options.A: At the end of every quarter

explanation: Prompt notification within 24 hours ensures that clinical details are fresh and records remain accurate before staff rotate or forget details. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h2)

question: A community health extension worker reports that a pregnant woman died at home after prolonged bleeding. How should the facility handle this event under MPDSR?

options.A: Report the family to the local police for failing to seek care
options.B: Ignore it because the patient never reached the hospital gates
options.C: Include it as a community-based maternal death notification for review
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to see if another similar case happens

explanation: MPDSR captures both facility and community deaths to understand delays in seeking and reaching care. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h2)

question: When analyzing a maternal death, what does the first delay refer to?

options.A: Delay in writing the final autopsy report
options.B: Delay in deciding to seek medical care
options.C: Delay in transporting the patient to the hospital
options.D: Delay in administering blood in the ward

explanation: The first delay involves the family or patient recognizing danger signs and making the choice to seek help. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of gathering case notes, drug charts, and lab results during an MPDSR audit?

options.A: To provide reading material for incoming midwifery students
options.B: To hide mistakes made by senior doctors from the health ministry
options.C: To calculate the monthly salary bonuses for the maternity unit staff
options.D: To reconstruct an accurate timeline of the clinical events that occurred

explanation: Reviewing all available records helps the audit team see exactly what happened at every stage of the patient's admission. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why must MPDSR audits maintain a strictly blame-free environment?

options.A: To ensure that doctors and midwives never face professional exams
options.B: To encourage honest reporting and prevent staff from hiding clinical errors
options.C: To stop patients from asking questions about their treatment plans
options.D: To allow healthcare workers to ignore hospital Standard Operating Procedures

explanation: When staff know they will not be punished for honest mistakes, they report deaths accurately and discuss system flaws openly. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following practices is essential for protecting patient and staff privacy during an audit?

options.A: Anonymizing names and personal identifiers in review documents
options.B: Publishing the full home addresses of deceased patients in local newspapers
options.C: Recording video footage of the audit meeting to share on social media
options.D: Requiring junior midwives to sign legal confessions for every bad outcome

explanation: Removing names protects patient confidentiality and keeps staff secure from unfair targeting. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h4)

question: What does the 'T' stand for in SMART recommendations formulated by an MPDSR committee?
explanation: SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound, ensuring deadlines are set for interventions. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following audit recommendations is written correctly according to MPDSR standards?

options.A: Find more money from somewhere to fix the broken roof in the antenatal clinic
options.B: Tell everyone to work harder so that mothers stop dying in our hospital this year
options.C: Procure ten functional delivery couches and train all labor ward staff on postpartum hemorrhage drills within six weeks
options.D: Advise doctors to be more careful whenever they perform a cesarean section

explanation: This recommendation is specific, actionable, and has a clear timeline, unlike vague statements that cannot be measured. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring implementation after an MPDSR audit?

options.A: To check if the recommendations successfully resolved the identified problems
options.B: To prove to international donors that the hospital has enough computers
options.C: To increase the amount of paperwork required for every maternity admission
options.D: To punish staff members who failed to attend the previous committee meeting

explanation: Monitoring ensures that action plans do not just sit on paper but lead to real changes in patient safety. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h6)

question: What helps sustain long-term quality improvement in a maternity unit following routine MPDSR audits?

options.A: Sharing feedback openly and providing continuous supportive supervision to staff
options.B: Keeping all audit committee discussions secret from the regular ward nurses
options.C: Stopping all review meetings once the maternal mortality rate drops slightly
options.D: Relying solely on disciplinary queries whenever a clinical complication arises

explanation: Open communication and supportive supervision keep the team engaged and committed to high standards of care. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h6)
